transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... honestly, I feel like I just cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I am completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still. Like yesterday, I tried to just sit on the couch, but then I remembered the pantry needed organizing. I started pulling out all the canned goods, and you wouldn't believe how many cans of crushed tomatoes I had pushed to the back. I used to make my own pasta sauce from scratch all the time back when my kids were still in high school. We'd have the whole neighborhood over for dinner on Sundays. The Johnsons next door always brought this terrible green jello salad with the carrots in it, but we smiled and ate it anyway to be polite. I wonder whatever happened to them... they had that little beagle that used to dig up my petunias out front. But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right. I just can't seem to sit down and rest, even when I'm dead on my feet.
Have you felt this way your entire life, or is this a relatively new experience for you?

Well, I mean, I've always been a bit of a busybody, you know? Always doing something. But... it hasn't always been this bad. It really started causing me real trouble, like, where I just can't stop myself, since my husband passed away. That was about... oh, a year and ten months ago now. Bless his heart, he used to be the one to tell me to sit down and put my feet up. We had this big, ugly brown recliner he bought at a garage sale back in '98. I hated that chair. I tried to throw it out three different times, but he always caught me. Once I even had the thrift store truck backed into the driveway, and he came home early from the hardware store. He was always going to the hardware store for something or other. He loved those little bins of screws and nails... but anyway, yes, it's been much, much worse since he's been gone.

Since your husband passed away, have you noticed any other changes, such as a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or perhaps feeling like you just don't have the energy to do things anymore?

Well, no, not really. I don't think I've lost interest in things. If anything, I want to do too many things all at once! And energy... oh, I have energy. Too much of it, like I was saying. I just keep going and going. I tried to take up knitting again to give my hands something to do while I watch TV. I used to knit all the time. I made this beautiful baby blanket for my oldest daughter when she was pregnant with my first grandson. It was this soft, pale yellow yarn because they didn't know if it was a boy or a girl. They wanted it to be a surprise, which I just think is so sweet. Nowadays everybody has those big parties with the pink or blue smoke, you know? I saw one on the news where they accidentally started a forest fire with one of those smoke things. Can you imagine? Just terrible. But, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm tired or sad like that. Just... revved up, I guess.
Since you have been feeling so revved up, have you found that you are able to get by on significantly less sleep than you usually need without feeling tired the next day?

Well, no, I wouldn't say I need less sleep. I mean, I still try to get my full eight hours, even if it takes me forever to actually fall asleep because my mind is just racing. But once I'm out, I'm out. It's funny you mention sleep, though, because my neighbor, Susan, she swears by that melatonin stuff. She buys the little gummy ones that taste like strawberries. I tried one once, but it just gave me the strangest dreams. I dreamt I was back in high school, trying to find my locker, but all the hallways were made of cheese. Swiss cheese, specifically, with the big holes in it. I remember thinking, "How am I supposed to walk on this?" And my old home ec teacher, Mrs. Gable, was there, just shaking her head at me. She was a strict one, Mrs. Gable. She failed me on my final project because my hem was crooked on the apron we had to sew. I was so upset, I cried all the way home on the bus. But anyway... no, I still need my sleep, I just have a hard time winding down to get it.
When your mind is racing, as you described, are you mostly preoccupied with specific worries or anxieties about various aspects of your life, or is it more of a general feeling of restlessness?

Well, it's not really worrying about things, no. It's more... well, honestly, it's the whole reason I finally came in to see you. I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's this awful restless feeling. Speaking of skin, I tried using that special Aveeno lotion, the one with the oatmeal? My sister Margaret swore by it when she had shingles last year. Oh, poor Margaret, she was in so much pain she couldn't even wear a blouse for two weeks, just had to walk around her house in a silk robe her husband bought her for their 25th anniversary. It was a beautiful robe, deep emerald green, with these little embroidered birds on the pockets. I always wanted one like it, but my husband wasn't much for buying clothes. He bought me a vacuum cleaner for our anniversary once. A Hoover. It was a good vacuum, lasted fifteen years, but still... not very romantic. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. The lotion didn't help me because it's not an itch, you know? It's just this constant urge. Like I have to jump up and do the next thing, whatever it is, right that very second. Even when I am just completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still and resting my feet, I just can't do it. I have to get up.
When you feel this restlessness, do you find yourself frequently worrying about things like your health, your finances, or your family's safety?

Well, no, not really. I don't sit around worrying about those kinds of things. My finances are fine, my husband saw to that before he passed. He was very good with money. He worked at the bank downtown for thirty-five years, started as a teller and worked his way up. He used to bring home those little lollipops they keep on the counter for the kids? The ones with the loop handles so they don't choke? I always thought that was such a smart invention. I wonder who came up with that. They probably made a fortune. I saw a show once about people who invented simple things like that, like the little plastic table they put in pizza boxes so the cheese doesn't stick to the lid. A woman invented that! I think her name was Carmela something. Or maybe it was Maria. Anyway, she lived in New York. I've never been to New York, but I'd love to see the Rockettes. My neighbor went last Christmas and she said it was just spectacular. But no, I don't really worry about my health or anything like that. It's just that awful restless feeling, like I was saying.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you cannot hear or see?

Oh, goodness no. I've never had anything like that happen. No voices or visions or anything of the sort. My aunt Mildred, though, she used to say she could see auras around people. She told me mine was a sort of pale yellow, like a buttercup. She had a whole garden full of buttercups at her old house in Ohio. It was a lovely little house, painted light blue with white shutters. She had this big oak tree in the front yard that had a tire swing on it. We used to swing on that thing for hours when we'd visit in the summer. My cousin Bobby fell off it once and broke his arm. He cried so loud the neighbors came running. They had a dog, the neighbors did, a big golden retriever named Buster. Buster was a good boy, he used to bring the morning paper right to their porch. I wish I had a dog like that. But no, I've never seen anything that wasn't really there. Just the regular things, you know?
When you feel this intense restlessness, do you ever notice physical sensations like your heart racing, feeling shaky, or sweating?

No, not at all. My heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or shaky or anything like that. It's just that feeling of having to move. Speaking of sweating, though, my goodness, the summers here have gotten so hot lately. I remember when I was a girl, we didn't even have air conditioning, just a big box fan in the window. We used to sit in front of it and make funny noises into the blades to hear our voices sound all robotic. My brother Tommy was the best at it. He could do a perfect imitation of that robot from Lost in Space. "Danger, Will Robinson!" he'd yell. He loved that show. He actually built a little robot out of cardboard boxes and aluminum foil for a science fair project once. He won second place. First place went to a girl who made a volcano that actually erupted with baking soda and vinegar. I always thought that was a bit of a cliché, you know? The volcano. But I suppose the judges liked it. Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, no, my heart is fine. No shaking or sweating. Just the restlessness.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt unusually 'high,' energetic, or irritable, perhaps even more than you feel right now?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, I have energy, but not like... not like some kind of strange high or anything for days on end. I'm just me, you know? Though, speaking of energy, my goodness, the hummingbirds at my feeder right now. Have you ever just watched a hummingbird? They are just go, go, go, all the time. Their little wings beat so fast you can barely see them. I read somewhere they have to eat constantly just to keep their hearts going. I make my own nectar for them, you know. Just sugar and water, no red dye. The red dye is bad for them, it can cause tumors or something. I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office. Dr. Henderson, he's been my dentist for twenty years. He has the gentlest hands. His son is taking over the practice now, though, and I'm not sure how I feel about that. The son always looks like he just woke up, his hair is always a mess. I don't know if I trust a dentist with messy hair. It seems like they should be very neat and tidy people, don't you think? Like a surgeon. You wouldn't want a messy surgeon. But anyway, no, no unusual highs or anything like that. Just the regular amount of energy, well, maybe a bit more restless energy like I said, but nothing crazy.
When you have this restless feeling, do you often experience any physical discomfort, such as muscle aches, tension in your neck or shoulders, or perhaps stomach upset?

No, I don't really get any of that. No aches or stomach problems when I get restless. I mean, my shoulders get a little stiff sometimes, but I think that's just from my mattress. It's getting kind of old, you know? It's one of those memory foam ones, and I think the memory is starting to fade. My daughter bought it for me about... oh, it must be eight years ago now. She ordered it online and it came rolled up in this tiny box. I couldn't believe a whole bed was in there. When we cut the plastic, it just expanded like a giant marshmallow. It was the funniest thing to watch. We laughed so hard we nearly cried. She's got such a good laugh, my daughter. She lives out in Oregon now, near Portland. It rains a lot there, she says, but the trees are just beautiful. She sent me a picture of this waterfall she hiked to last weekend, Multnomah Falls, I think it was called. It looked like something out of a fairy tale. I'd love to visit her soon, but I just don't know if I could sit still on a plane for that long. It's a five-hour flight, and you're just trapped in those little seats. The last time I flew, the man next to me fell asleep and kept leaning on my shoulder. He was snoring, too. I didn't want to wake him, but it was terribly uncomfortable. So, no, no stomach aches or muscle tension from the restlessness, just the regular kind from sleeping funny or sitting too long.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, perhaps for high blood pressure, stomach issues, or your mood?

No, I don't take anything like that. No prescriptions at all right now. Just a multivitamin in the morning, the kind with the extra calcium for women my age. Oh, and sometimes I'll take a little melatonin if I really can't get to sleep, but that's just from the drugstore. The drugstore down the street from me, the one on Elm, they just remodeled the whole inside. It used to be so dark and cramped, but now they've got these bright fluorescent lights and the aisles are so wide you could drive a golf cart down them. I don't know why they need so much space for greeting cards, though. Whole rows of them. Who buys that many cards anymore? Everyone just sends a text message or puts something on Facebook. I tried to get on Facebook to see pictures of my daughter's dog—she got a golden retriever mix, a rescue, such a sweet face—but I kept forgetting my password. They make you use a capital letter and a number and a symbol now. An exclamation point or a dollar sign. It's too much to remember. I wrote it down on a sticky note, but then the sticky note lost its stick and fell behind the desk. I tried to fish it out with a wire hanger, but I just ended up pulling out a bunch of dust bunnies. You wouldn't believe the dust that gathers back there. It's like a whole other ecosystem. But anyway, no, no medications for blood pressure or stomach things or anything like that. Just the vitamins.
Does this restless feeling cause you significant distress or make it difficult for you to carry out your daily activities?

Well, yes... it really does. It's actually gotten quite bad. I mean, my family has had to step in and take over my bills and all my paperwork because I just can't sit still long enough to get through it all. My daughter put everything on that auto-pay thing on the computer. It makes me a little nervous, to be honest, just letting the machine take the money out of the bank. What if they make a mistake? I saw on the local news about a woman who got charged ten thousand dollars for her water bill just because of a computer glitch. Ten thousand dollars! I don't even use that much water, except maybe in the summer for the community garden. 

But even there... the people at the garden, and at my church too, they've had to step in and redo plans or cover responsibilities that I just completely dropped. I was supposed to organize the spring planting schedule, and I just couldn't get it done. Speaking of spring, the daffodils came up so early this year. Have you noticed? The bright yellow ones right by the church steps are already blooming. Reverend Thomas says it's because of the mild winter. He's a very nice man, always wears these brightly colored ties. His wife knits them, I think. Or maybe she weaves them. I tried knitting once, but I kept dropping stitches and my scarf ended up looking like a lopsided triangle. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the distress. Yes, it's just so embarrassing. I feel awful because these groups I really care about, it feels like they just don't think they can count on me anymore. It's a terrible feeling to let people down like that.
Have you ever found yourself doing things on the spur of the moment, like spending money you didn't have or taking unnecessary risks, that you later regretted?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I've always been pretty careful with my money, especially since I stopped working. You have to be, you know? On a fixed income, every penny counts. I clip coupons still, even though they're mostly digital now. The grocery store app is a nightmare to navigate. You have to "clip" them on your phone before you go in. I stood in the produce section for ten minutes last week trying to get twenty cents off a bag of apples. They were Honeycrisp, though, and those are always so expensive. But they're the best for making pies. My grandmother used to make the most wonderful apple pie from scratch. She had this old rolling pin that was heavier than a brick, carved out of some dark wood... cherry, maybe? Or mahogany. She said it was the weight that made the crust so flaky. I still have it in my kitchen drawer, actually, right next to the potato masher that always gets stuck when you try to open it. Don't you hate that? When a drawer jams because of one utensil? It's usually the ladle for me. But anyway, no, I don't go out and spend money I don't have or do anything risky like that. I just stick to my budget and try to find the good apples when they're on sale.
Do you often find that you have trouble staying focused on a task or that you frequently lose things like your keys or your glasses?

Well, yes, I suppose I do have a lot of trouble with that. I can sit down with the senior center newsletter, or even the choir schedule for church, and I start out just fine. But then, after a few minutes, I realize my eyes have just gone over the same lines three or four times and I have absolutely no idea what I just read. It's like the words just float right off the page. The newsletter is printed on this very strange paper now, anyway. It's glossy, almost like a magazine, which makes it terrible if you want to circle something with a pen. The ink just smears right off onto your hand. I got ink all over my good beige cardigan last week trying to circle the date for the potluck. It's a shame, too, because I bought that cardigan at a little boutique downtown that closed years ago. The woman who ran it, Sylvia, she always had the most beautiful glass buttons on her sweaters. She moved to Florida, I think. Or maybe Arizona? Somewhere warm for her arthritis. My own knees ache when it rains, but it hasn't rained in weeks. The grass in my front yard is starting to look like shredded wheat. I try to water it, but dragging the hose around is just such a chore. But yes, I just can't seem to keep my mind on what I'm reading or doing for very long at all.

patient.answer: Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... honestly, I feel like I just cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I am completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still. Like yesterday, I tried to just sit on the couch, but then I remembered the pantry needed organizing. I started pulling out all the canned goods, and you wouldn't believe how many cans of crushed tomatoes I had pushed to the back. I used to make my own pasta sauce from scratch all the time back when my kids were still in high school. We'd have the whole neighborhood over for dinner on Sundays. The Johnsons next door always brought this terrible green jello salad with the carrots in it, but we smiled and ate it anyway to be polite. I wonder whatever happened to them... they had that little beagle that used to dig up my petunias out front. But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right. I just can't seem to sit down and rest, even when I'm dead on my feet.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between a primary mood/anxiety disorder and an adjustment disorder by assessing if the symptoms are causing significant impairment or distress in areas beyond just the inability to relax.
doctor.question: Since your husband passed away, have you noticed any other changes, such as a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or perhaps feeling like you just don't have the energy to do things anymore?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressive symptoms (loss of interest, lack of energy), which are not covered by any of the ADHD-specific symptom profiles provided.

patient.answer: Well, no, not really. I don't think I've lost interest in things. If anything, I want to do too many things all at once! And energy... oh, I have energy. Too much of it, like I was saying. I just keep going and going. I tried to take up knitting again to give my hands something to do while I watch TV. I used to knit all the time. I made this beautiful baby blanket for my oldest daughter when she was pregnant with my first grandson. It was this soft, pale yellow yarn because they didn't know if it was a boy or a girl. They wanted it to be a surprise, which I just think is so sweet. Nowadays everybody has those big parties with the pink or blue smoke, you know? I saw one on the news where they accidentally started a forest fire with one of those smoke things. Can you imagine? Just terrible. But, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm tired or sad like that. Just... revved up, I guess.

inference.note: The patient's report of excessive energy, 'revved up' feeling, and difficulty sitting still, combined with the absence of depressive symptoms, shifts the differential away from depressive or simple adjustment disorders and toward potential manic or hypomanic symptoms, or anxiety.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between manic/hypomanic symptoms (F30.1, F30.9) and anxiety/adjustment-related symptoms (F41.1, F43.24) by checking for a decreased need for sleep.
doctor.question: Since you have been feeling so revved up, have you found that you are able to get by on significantly less sleep than you usually need without feeling tired the next day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a decreased need for sleep, which is a symptom of mania and is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Well, no, I wouldn't say I need less sleep. I mean, I still try to get my full eight hours, even if it takes me forever to actually fall asleep because my mind is just racing. But once I'm out, I'm out. It's funny you mention sleep, though, because my neighbor, Susan, she swears by that melatonin stuff. She buys the little gummy ones that taste like strawberries. I tried one once, but it just gave me the strangest dreams. I dreamt I was back in high school, trying to find my locker, but all the hallways were made of cheese. Swiss cheese, specifically, with the big holes in it. I remember thinking, "How am I supposed to walk on this?" And my old home ec teacher, Mrs. Gable, was there, just shaking her head at me. She was a strict one, Mrs. Gable. She failed me on my final project because my hem was crooked on the apron we had to sew. I was so upset, I cried all the way home on the bus. But anyway... no, I still need my sleep, I just have a hard time winding down to get it.

inference.note: The patient's report of not needing less sleep and not having elevated mood makes F30.1 and F30.9 (manic episode) much less likely. I have replaced them with F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with anxiety), as her symptoms of restlessness and racing thoughts are occurring in the context of bereavement.

doctor.intent: Differentiate between Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and Adjustment Disorder (F43.2) by checking for excessive worry about a variety of events or activities.
doctor.question: When your mind is racing, as you described, are you mostly preoccupied with specific worries or anxieties about various aspects of your life, or is it more of a general feeling of restlessness?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore, like I have to jump up and do the next thing even when I am worn out and should be sitting still.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether my racing mind is driven by specific worries (anxiety) or a general feeling of restlessness, which directly relates to my symptom of feeling restless.

patient.answer:
Well, it's not really worrying about things, no. It's more... well, honestly, it's the whole reason I finally came in to see you. I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's this awful restless feeling. Speaking of skin, I tried using that special Aveeno lotion, the one with the oatmeal? My sister Margaret swore by it when she had shingles last year. Oh, poor Margaret, she was in so much pain she couldn't even wear a blouse for two weeks, just had to walk around her house in a silk robe her husband bought her for their 25th anniversary. It was a beautiful robe, deep emerald green, with these little embroidered birds on the pockets. I always wanted one like it, but my husband wasn't much for buying clothes. He bought me a vacuum cleaner for our anniversary once. A Hoover. It was a good vacuum, lasted fifteen years, but still... not very romantic. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. The lotion didn't help me because it's not an itch, you know? It's just this constant urge. Like I have to jump up and do the next thing, whatever it is, right that very second. Even when I am just completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still and resting my feet, I just can't do it. I have to get up.

inference.note: The patient's persistent, non-anxious physical restlessness (akathisia-like feeling without medication usage) and difficulty winding down, in the absence of primary depressive symptoms or classic panic, suggests considering somatic symptom disorders or generalized anxiety; F43.24 was removed as the symptoms are not primarily depressive.

doctor.intent: To differentiate between Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and Adjustment Disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22) by assessing the presence of persistent, excessive worry about multiple life domains.
doctor.question: When you feel this restlessness, do you find yourself frequently worrying about things like your health, your finances, or your family's safety?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about excessive worry regarding specific domains like health, finances, or family safety, which is a symptom of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. My symptom profile only contains ADHD symptoms and does not include excessive worrying.

patient.answer: Well, no, not really. I don't sit around worrying about those kinds of things. My finances are fine, my husband saw to that before he passed. He was very good with money. He worked at the bank downtown for thirty-five years, started as a teller and worked his way up. He used to bring home those little lollipops they keep on the counter for the kids? The ones with the loop handles so they don't choke? I always thought that was such a smart invention. I wonder who came up with that. They probably made a fortune. I saw a show once about people who invented simple things like that, like the little plastic table they put in pizza boxes so the cheese doesn't stick to the lid. A woman invented that! I think her name was Carmela something. Or maybe it was Maria. Anyway, she lived in New York. I've never been to New York, but I'd love to see the Rockettes. My neighbor went last Christmas and she said it was just spectacular. But no, I don't really worry about my health or anything like that. It's just that awful restless feeling, like I was saying.

inference.note: The patient's persistent, intense, and non-anxious physical restlessness, accompanied by a tangential, circumstantial, and slightly pressured flow of speech, necessitates considering conditions involving hypomanic or psychomotor agitation, in addition to generalized anxiety.

doctor.intent: To determine if the patient experiences perceptual disturbances or formal thought disorder, which would help differentiate F25.0 (Schizoaffective Disorder) from the other candidates.
doctor.question: Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you cannot hear or see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hallucinations (hearing or seeing things others cannot), which is not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Oh, goodness no. I've never had anything like that happen. No voices or visions or anything of the sort. My aunt Mildred, though, she used to say she could see auras around people. She told me mine was a sort of pale yellow, like a buttercup. She had a whole garden full of buttercups at her old house in Ohio. It was a lovely little house, painted light blue with white shutters. She had this big oak tree in the front yard that had a tire swing on it. We used to swing on that thing for hours when we'd visit in the summer. My cousin Bobby fell off it once and broke his arm. He cried so loud the neighbors came running. They had a dog, the neighbors did, a big golden retriever named Buster. Buster was a good boy, he used to bring the morning paper right to their porch. I wish I had a dog like that. But no, I've never seen anything that wasn't really there. Just the regular things, you know?

inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation of persistent motor restlessness, lack of cognitive symptoms of mania (racing thoughts are not goal-directed, no decreased need for sleep), and absence of psychotic features suggests that F25.0 and F34.0 are unlikely. F41.1 remains a possibility for generalized anxiety, but the physical nature of the restlessness points toward potential somatoform or other specified neurotic disorders.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and somatic symptom-related issues by checking for physical symptoms of autonomic arousal (e.g., heart racing, sweating, trembling) that often accompany anxiety.
doctor.question: When you feel this intense restlessness, do you ever notice physical sensations like your heart racing, feeling shaky, or sweating?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about physical symptoms of anxiety or panic attacks, such as a racing heart, shakiness, or sweating, which are not covered by my ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, not at all. My heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or shaky or anything like that. It's just that feeling of having to move. Speaking of sweating, though, my goodness, the summers here have gotten so hot lately. I remember when I was a girl, we didn't even have air conditioning, just a big box fan in the window. We used to sit in front of it and make funny noises into the blades to hear our voices sound all robotic. My brother Tommy was the best at it. He could do a perfect imitation of that robot from Lost in Space. "Danger, Will Robinson!" he'd yell. He loved that show. He actually built a little robot out of cardboard boxes and aluminum foil for a science fair project once. He won second place. First place went to a girl who made a volcano that actually erupted with baking soda and vinegar. I always thought that was a bit of a cliché, you know? The volcano. But I suppose the judges liked it. Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, no, my heart is fine. No shaking or sweating. Just the restlessness.

inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation of constant physical restlessness ('cannot settle inside my own skin') without autonomic arousal (no heart racing, sweating, or shaking) or cognitive anxiety/worry makes GAD (F41.1) less likely. The persistent, pervasive nature of this restlessness, combined with the patient's tangential and circumstantial speech patterns, suggests a need to consider personality-related issues (F60.3) or undifferentiated somatoform/restlessness patterns.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced significant mood swings or periods of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood that could indicate a manic or hypomanic episode (F60.3), as opposed to anxiety or somatic symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt unusually 'high,' energetic, or irritable, perhaps even more than you feel right now?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of mania or hypomania (feeling unusually high, energetic, or irritable for several days), which is not part of my ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I can't say I have. I mean, I have energy, but not like... not like some kind of strange high or anything for days on end. I'm just me, you know? Though, speaking of energy, my goodness, the hummingbirds at my feeder right now. Have you ever just watched a hummingbird? They are just go, go, go, all the time. Their little wings beat so fast you can barely see them. I read somewhere they have to eat constantly just to keep their hearts going. I make my own nectar for them, you know. Just sugar and water, no red dye. The red dye is bad for them, it can cause tumors or something. I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office. Dr. Henderson, he's been my dentist for twenty years. He has the gentlest hands. His son is taking over the practice now, though, and I'm not sure how I feel about that. The son always looks like he just woke up, his hair is always a mess. I don't know if I trust a dentist with messy hair. It seems like they should be very neat and tidy people, don't you think? Like a surgeon. You wouldn't want a messy surgeon. But anyway, no, no unusual highs or anything like that. Just the regular amount of energy, well, maybe a bit more restless energy like I said, but nothing crazy.

inference.note: The patient's presentation of persistent, non-episodic restlessness without autonomic symptoms or cognitive distortions related to anxiety, and the absence of mood episodes, makes F60.3 less likely. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) is now considered due to the focus on persistent restlessness and 'racing mind' despite the patient's denial of classic worry.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has any somatic symptoms (e.g., muscle tension, digestive issues) that could point toward a somatoform disorder (F45.8) versus generalized anxiety or unspecified restlessness.
doctor.question: When you have this restless feeling, do you often experience any physical discomfort, such as muscle aches, tension in your neck or shoulders, or perhaps stomach upset?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about somatic symptoms of anxiety, such as muscle tension or stomach upset, which are not covered by my ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't really get any of that. No aches or stomach problems when I get restless. I mean, my shoulders get a little stiff sometimes, but I think that's just from my mattress. It's getting kind of old, you know? It's one of those memory foam ones, and I think the memory is starting to fade. My daughter bought it for me about... oh, it must be eight years ago now. She ordered it online and it came rolled up in this tiny box. I couldn't believe a whole bed was in there. When we cut the plastic, it just expanded like a giant marshmallow. It was the funniest thing to watch. We laughed so hard we nearly cried. She's got such a good laugh, my daughter. She lives out in Oregon now, near Portland. It rains a lot there, she says, but the trees are just beautiful. She sent me a picture of this waterfall she hiked to last weekend, Multnomah Falls, I think it was called. It looked like something out of a fairy tale. I'd love to visit her soon, but I just don't know if I could sit still on a plane for that long. It's a five-hour flight, and you're just trapped in those little seats. The last time I flew, the man next to me fell asleep and kept leaning on my shoulder. He was snoring, too. I didn't want to wake him, but it was terribly uncomfortable. So, no, no stomach aches or muscle tension from the restlessness, just the regular kind from sleeping funny or sitting too long.

inference.note: Added F20.89 (Other schizophreniform disorders) to account for the patient's prominent tangentiality and flight of ideas, which might point toward a formal thought disorder rather than just anxiety or somatic symptoms.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient is taking any medications that could cause akathisia (drug-induced restlessness).
doctor.question: Are you currently taking any prescription medications, perhaps for high blood pressure, stomach issues, or your mood?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about current prescription medications, which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't take anything like that. No prescriptions at all right now. Just a multivitamin in the morning, the kind with the extra calcium for women my age. Oh, and sometimes I'll take a little melatonin if I really can't get to sleep, but that's just from the drugstore. The drugstore down the street from me, the one on Elm, they just remodeled the whole inside. It used to be so dark and cramped, but now they've got these bright fluorescent lights and the aisles are so wide you could drive a golf cart down them. I don't know why they need so much space for greeting cards, though. Whole rows of them. Who buys that many cards anymore? Everyone just sends a text message or puts something on Facebook. I tried to get on Facebook to see pictures of my daughter's dog—she got a golden retriever mix, a rescue, such a sweet face—but I kept forgetting my password. They make you use a capital letter and a number and a symbol now. An exclamation point or a dollar sign. It's too much to remember. I wrote it down on a sticky note, but then the sticky note lost its stick and fell behind the desk. I tried to fish it out with a wire hanger, but I just ended up pulling out a bunch of dust bunnies. You wouldn't believe the dust that gathers back there. It's like a whole other ecosystem. But anyway, no, no medications for blood pressure or stomach things or anything like that. Just the vitamins.

inference.note: The patient's excessive circumstantiality, tangentiality, and loose associations, combined with her persistent restlessness, suggest the need to consider schizotypal personality disorder (F21) as a diagnostic possibility, alongside the previously considered anxiety and somatoform-related conditions.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a somatic symptom that causes distress or functional impairment, which is a key diagnostic criterion for F45.8 (Other Somatic Symptom Disorder).
doctor.question: Does this restless feeling cause you significant distress or make it difficult for you to carry out your daily activities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My family has had to step in with bills and paperwork, and people at church and the garden have had to redo plans or cover responsibilities I dropped. I feel embarrassed because groups I care about no longer feel they can count on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the restless feeling causes significant distress or makes it difficult to carry out daily activities, which directly addresses the functional impairment caused by the symptoms.

patient.answer:
Well, yes... it really does. It's actually gotten quite bad. I mean, my family has had to step in and take over my bills and all my paperwork because I just can't sit still long enough to get through it all. My daughter put everything on that auto-pay thing on the computer. It makes me a little nervous, to be honest, just letting the machine take the money out of the bank. What if they make a mistake? I saw on the local news about a woman who got charged ten thousand dollars for her water bill just because of a computer glitch. Ten thousand dollars! I don't even use that much water, except maybe in the summer for the community garden. 

But even there... the people at the garden, and at my church too, they've had to step in and redo plans or cover responsibilities that I just completely dropped. I was supposed to organize the spring planting schedule, and I just couldn't get it done. Speaking of spring, the daffodils came up so early this year. Have you noticed? The bright yellow ones right by the church steps are already blooming. Reverend Thomas says it's because of the mild winter. He's a very nice man, always wears these brightly colored ties. His wife knits them, I think. Or maybe she weaves them. I tried knitting once, but I kept dropping stitches and my scarf ended up looking like a lopsided triangle. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the distress. Yes, it's just so embarrassing. I feel awful because these groups I really care about, it feels like they just don't think they can count on me anymore. It's a terrible feeling to let people down like that.

inference.note: The patient's lifelong history of being a 'busybody' combined with the recent significant impairment in executive function (inability to handle finances or commitments) and persistent motor restlessness suggests looking into adult ADHD (F90.0) or personality-related dysregulation (F60.2/F60.3) rather than just anxiety or somatization.

doctor.intent: To determine if the patient has a history of impulsive or reckless behaviors that would support a diagnosis of F60.2 (Antisocial Personality Disorder) versus F90.0 (ADHD).
doctor.question: Have you ever found yourself doing things on the spur of the moment, like spending money you didn't have or taking unnecessary risks, that you later regretted?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about impulsive behaviors such as spending money recklessly or taking unnecessary risks, which are not covered by any of the specific ADHD symptoms in my profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't really do anything like that. I've always been pretty careful with my money, especially since I stopped working. You have to be, you know? On a fixed income, every penny counts. I clip coupons still, even though they're mostly digital now. The grocery store app is a nightmare to navigate. You have to "clip" them on your phone before you go in. I stood in the produce section for ten minutes last week trying to get twenty cents off a bag of apples. They were Honeycrisp, though, and those are always so expensive. But they're the best for making pies. My grandmother used to make the most wonderful apple pie from scratch. She had this old rolling pin that was heavier than a brick, carved out of some dark wood... cherry, maybe? Or mahogany. She said it was the weight that made the crust so flaky. I still have it in my kitchen drawer, actually, right next to the potato masher that always gets stuck when you try to open it. Don't you hate that? When a drawer jams because of one utensil? It's usually the ladle for me. But anyway, no, I don't go out and spend money I don't have or do anything risky like that. I just stick to my budget and try to find the good apples when they're on sale.

inference.note: The patient's significant distress and impairment in daily functioning, combined with persistent, non-episodic restlessness and difficulty focusing, makes Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) a strong candidate, while the lifelong history of being a 'busybody' and current inability to sit still supports keeping F90.0. The lack of mood-related episodes effectively rules out F60.3.

doctor.intent: Assess if the patient exhibits consistent signs of inattention or forgetfulness in daily life, which would support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.0) over GAD (F41.1).
doctor.question: Do you often find that you have trouble staying focused on a task or that you frequently lose things like your keys or your glasses?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I can sit down with the senior center newsletter or a choir schedule and start out fine, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes have gone over the same lines and I have no idea what I just read.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have trouble staying focused on a task, which directly corresponds to the symptom of difficulty sustaining attention.

patient.answer: Well, yes, I suppose I do have a lot of trouble with that. I can sit down with the senior center newsletter, or even the choir schedule for church, and I start out just fine. But then, after a few minutes, I realize my eyes have just gone over the same lines three or four times and I have absolutely no idea what I just read. It's like the words just float right off the page. The newsletter is printed on this very strange paper now, anyway. It's glossy, almost like a magazine, which makes it terrible if you want to circle something with a pen. The ink just smears right off onto your hand. I got ink all over my good beige cardigan last week trying to circle the date for the potluck. It's a shame, too, because I bought that cardigan at a little boutique downtown that closed years ago. The woman who ran it, Sylvia, she always had the most beautiful glass buttons on her sweaters. She moved to Florida, I think. Or maybe Arizona? Somewhere warm for her arthritis. My own knees ache when it rains, but it hasn't rained in weeks. The grass in my front yard is starting to look like shredded wheat. I try to water it, but dragging the hose around is just such a chore. But yes, I just can't seem to keep my mind on what I'm reading or doing for very long at all.

inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation of lifelong 'busybody' behavior, severe difficulty with sustained attention and task completion (forgetting, losing track of reading, inability to follow through on commitments), and chronic restlessness, combined with the absence of episodic mood symptoms or anxiety-related physical symptoms, strongly supports an adult ADHD diagnosis and effectively rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1).

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the primary reason for the patient's visit.
opening_question.question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent, pervasive symptoms of restlessness and inability to focus that impair her daily functioning. While she describes these as worsening later in life, her history of being a 'busybody' and current manifestation of inattention, inability to complete tasks, and motor restlessness (need to keep moving) align with an ADHD presentation. Other conditions like Generalized Anxiety Disorder were ruled out due to lack of specific worry/anxiety themes and absence of physiological arousal (heart racing/sweating).
